messages:
alex_w: quick async — opened a TF PR to adjust VPC peering routes and flip dev NAT to NAT Gateway w/ ephemeral EIP pool. need a quick sanity check before i split it up. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/542

maya: skimmed the diff, looks reasonable at a glance. one concern: route table association order when peering is replaced. might need an explicit depends_on to avoid transient blackholes :eyes:

alex_w: good call. i added depends_on on the route resource pointing at the peering connection. snippet from module: 
```
resource "aws_route" "peer_prod" {
  route_table_id            = var.route_table_id
  destination_cidr_block    = aws_vpc.prod.cidr_block
  vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering_connection.peer.id
  depends_on                = [aws_vpc_peering_connection.peer]
}
```

samir: quick Q — you're switching dev NAT instances -> nat gateway with EIPs? if these EIPs are ephemeral we need tagging/reuse logic or we'll hit org EIP quota quickly. also lifecycle create_before_destroy for nat gateway?

alex_w: right — module now provisions aws_nat_gateway + aws_eip with a small `create_before_destroy` lifecycle on the nat gateway association. plan shows: 
```
+ aws_eip.dev_nat_eip (new)
+ aws_nat_gateway.dev_nat (new)
- aws_instance.dev_nat (destroy)
```

infra-bot: CI: terraform fmt failed in modules/vpc/routes/main.tf — please run `terraform fmt` and push. :warning:

maya: nit — run `tf fmt` and also confirm PrivateLink endpoint for secrets-manager is created in the same subnets/AZs as the consumer to avoid cross-AZ egress charges. did you add the interface endpoint?

alex_w: added aws_vpc_endpoint.secret_manager with subnet_ids = var.private_subnet_ids. code: 
```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "secrets_mgr" {
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.${data.aws_region.current.name}.secretsmanager"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids   = var.private_subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [var.endpoint_sg_id]
}
```

tj: suggestion — split this into two PRs: (A) peering + routes, (B) NAT/EIP + PrivateLink. makes rollback smaller and CI faster.

alex_w: i was leaning that way. i'll split into two branches tonight. will also add a lightweight smoke check in CI to run `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=${var.vpc_id}` so we at least validate presence of the nat gateway post-apply in staging.

samir: FYI we hit soft EIP limits last quarter for infra account, might need a quota increase if we allocate >5 new EIPs across accounts. i'll open a support request with AWS if PR ends up needing many EIPs.

alex_w: thanks — i'll coordinate. tagging @maya @tj for approvals once i split and fix the fmt. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: PR #542 split branches created: pr/542-peering and pr/542-nat. pipeline: queued.

maya: thanks. ping here when CI is green and i'll review the peering PR.
